title: Noncentral split torus gives a proper minimal rational parabolic
statement: Let $k$ be any field [def-weil-field] and let $G$ be a reductive $k$-group [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sfb-reductive-torus-centralizer-terminology]: smooth, affine of finite type and geometrically connected, with no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup after extension to an algebraic closure. Unipotent means admitting a faithful finite-dimensional matrix representation in which all geometric points are unipotent matrices. A split torus is a group scheme isomorphic over $k$ to $\mathbf G_{m,k}^r$, $r\geq0$, where $\mathbf G_{m,k}=\operatorname{Spec}k[z,z^{-1}]$ with multiplication of units. A parabolic $k$-subgroup $P\subseteq G$ means a smooth geometrically connected closed subgroup [def-weil-closed-immersion] whose fppf right-coset sheaf $G/P$ is represented by a proper finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Here the coset sheaf is the sheafification of $A\mapsto G(A)/P(A)$ for faithfully flat finitely presented coverings of commutative $k$-algebras, and $G(A)=\operatorname{Hom}_k(\operatorname{Spec}A,G)$. A minimal parabolic is one containing no strictly smaller parabolic $k$-subgroup; proper means $P\ne G$. Let $T\subseteq G$ be a closed split torus which is noncentral: for some commutative $k$-algebra $A$, some $t\in T(A)$ and some $g\in G(A)$ one has $tg\ne gt$. Then $G$ contains a proper minimal parabolic $k$-subgroup. This holds over finite and imperfect fields as well.

source.place: Proposition 25.2, printed p.545 (noncentral, not merely nontrivial, split torus); Section 25(a), Theorems 25.1 and 25.8, pp.544--546 (minimal rational parabolics). Minimality is obtained by choosing a proper parabolic of least dimension; all parabolics are smooth geometrically connected.

proof.text: Choose a $k$-isomorphism $T\simeq\mathbf G_m^r$. Its coordinate inclusions give cocharacters $\lambda_i:\mathbf G_m\to G$. For every test algebra $A$ and $(a_1,\ldots,a_r)\in T(A)$, its image in $G(A)$ equals $\prod_i\lambda_i(a_i)$. If each $\lambda_i$ commuted with every element of $G$ after every test-algebra extension, this product would commute too. Noncentrality of $T$ therefore gives one $\lambda=\lambda_i$ that is noncentral as a subgroup functor. In particular $r>0$.

source.place: Proposition 25.2, p.545: passing from a noncentral split torus to a noncentral coordinate cocharacter.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-reductive-cocharacter-parabolic-geometry] to this $k$-cocharacter $\lambda$. It gives the smooth geometrically connected closed subgroup $P_\lambda\subseteq G$ and represents its fppf coset sheaf by a smooth projective scheme $X_\lambda$. By [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper], $X_\lambda$ is proper, hence finite type by the definition of properness in [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Thus $P_\lambda$ is a parabolic with exactly the quotient convention of the statement.

source.place: Theorem 25.1, p.544 (parabolic quotient), as supplied in the existing cocharacter-geometry statement; projective implies proper as in Stacks Tag 01WC, lemma-locally-projective-proper.

proof.text: Suppose $P_\lambda=G$. The same cocharacter-geometry statement makes $U_\lambda$ a smooth geometrically connected normal subgroup of $G$, gives a split series $U_\lambda=U_0\supseteq\cdots\supseteq U_n=1$ of smooth closed subgroups, each normal in its predecessor with represented fppf quotient $\mathbf G_a$, and gives $G\simeq U_\lambda\rtimes Z_\lambda$; all of this commutes with extension to an algebraic closure $\bar k$ (smoothness, flatness, surjectivity, local finite presentation and scheme-theoretic kernels are preserved by this base change). Over $\bar k$ the trivial group is unipotent and $\mathbf G_a$ is unipotent via $x\mapsto\begin{pmatrix}1&x\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$, so descending induction on $j$, applying [lem-sfb-smooth-unipotent-extension] to $U_{j+1,\bar k}\subseteq U_{j,\bar k}\to\mathbf G_{a,\bar k}$, shows that $U_{\lambda,\bar k}$ is unipotent. It is smooth, connected and normal in $P_{\lambda,\bar k}=G_{\bar k}$, so reductivity forces $U_{\lambda,\bar k}=1$, and the decomposition gives $G_{\bar k}=Z_{\lambda,\bar k}$. This equality descends to $k$: the ideal defining the closed subgroup $Z_\lambda\subseteq G$ becomes zero after tensoring with $\bar k$, and a $k$-vector space injects into its scalar extension (extend any nonzero vector to a basis). Thus $G=Z_\lambda$. The functorial definition of $Z_\lambda$ in the cited statement says precisely that all elements commute with $\lambda$ after all algebra extensions, contradicting step 1. Hence $P_\lambda\ne G$.

source.place: Proposition 25.2, p.545: reductivity kills the normal unipotent kernel when P(lambda)=G; Theorem 13.33(b), pp.265-266; split unipotent groups are unipotent, Corollary 14.7 / Proposition 17.60.

proof.text: Write $G=\operatorname{Spec}R$, with $R$ a finitely generated $k$-algebra. By [lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components], descending chains of closed subsets of $G$ stabilize. Consider the nonempty collection of closed supports of parabolic $k$-subgroups contained in $P_\lambda$; it contains the support of $P_\lambda$. Choose a minimal member, represented by a parabolic $P\subseteq P_\lambda$: otherwise repeated strict descent would produce a nonstabilizing descending chain. If $Q\subseteq P$ is another parabolic of $G$, its support belongs to the same collection and therefore equals that of $P$. Both $P$ and $Q$ are smooth over $k$, hence reduced by [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced] applied to their structural morphisms. Uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] now gives equality of their defining ideal sheaves in $G$, so $Q=P$ as closed subgroup schemes. Thus $P$ is minimal among all parabolics of $G$, and $P\subseteq P_\lambda\ne G$ makes it proper. No step assumes that $k$ is infinite or perfect.

source.place: Section 25(a), pp.544-546: minimal parabolics; Noetherian closed-support choice and reduced-subscheme uniqueness, Stacks Tag 056T (lemma-smooth-geometrically-normal) and Tag 01J3 (lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme).
